objective: Extend the mesh gates with an advisory aspect-ratio rule and a volume-ratio warning, wired from the new mesh_quality section of the governed physics rules
rationale: The two hard gates the lab enforces, non-orthogonality 70 degrees and skewness 4, are exactly the acceptance thresholds compiled into checkMesh and stay unchanged. Two defensible gates are missing. Aspect ratio must enter as advisory only: the NASA TMR flat-plate reference grids on disk measure max aspect ratio 66643 to 74041 with zero non-orthogonality and machine-precision skewness, so a hard gate at the checkMesh reporting threshold of 1000 would reject every reference-grade boundary-layer grid; the defensible rule flags high aspect ratio only when it coincides with non-orthogonality above 60 degrees or skewness above 2. Volume ratio gets a warning below 0.01, the snappyHexMesh generation floor, catching abrupt cell-size jumps at refinement boundaries. Values and citations are already recorded in the governed physics rules under the mesh-quality section; this proposal is the enforcement wiring and the certificate note. The calibrated gate summary may also land directly as content on the mesh surfaces.
citations: OpenFOAM v2606 Source, SnappyHexMesh MeshQualityDict Defaults
NASA Turbulence Modeling Resource Flat-Plate Grids, CheckMesh Reports On Disk
expected_knowledge_gain: Every mesh the lab admits carries the same two hard gates as today plus a context-aware aspect-ratio judgment and a growth-rate warning, each traceable to a cited threshold rather than a habit
